newsitem.title: BULGARIA: ILL-PAID BULGARIA POLICE HELP MAFIA THRIVE - MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: ILL-PAID BULGARIA POLICE HELP MAFIA THRIVE - MINISTER.

text.p: Corruption and low motivation among poorly paid Bulgarian police officers are hindering efforts to fight organised crime, Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev said on Friday.

"We have to admit that we have only limited success in establishing the perpetrators of serious crimes like contract killings and trafficking of stolen cars as our officers have low motivation and out of date equipment and some of them are corrupt," Dobrev told a news conference.
Between January 1995 and September 30, 1996, 744 successful premeditated murders were committed in Bulgaria, but only 545 cases have been solved, interior ministry figures show.
During the same period, 4,391 cars were stolen, of which 3,079 have been found.
"We have limited resources and our task of protecting society is very difficult as now people prefer to keep their savings in cash at home," Dobrev said.
The slide of the lev against the dollar has made a lot of Bulgarians withdraw their lev savings from commercial banks and change them for dollars.

"We can hardly reach the big bosses of the organised crime groups as they have their sources in the ministry's structure and whenever we get closer to someone of the criminal top brass they set up some minor criminal who is paid to take the whole guilt and go to jail instead of his boss," Dobrev said.
He said the interior ministry planned to propose to parliament a draft law setting up a witness protection programme.
Bulgaria's crime rate has soared since the collapse of communism in 1989 as the small Balkan country moves slowly towards a market economy.

Former prime minister Andrei Lukanov was shot dead outside his home on October 2 in an apparent contract killing. The gun was found hidden behind a radiator in the entrance hall of a nearby apartment building but no one was been arrested.
